name: queryhost
description: Check public game-server status and compare player counts, maps, versions, and query response times with QueryHost.

interface.longDescription: Check a public game server by its hostname or IP address, or compare two to four servers in chat. QueryHost supports Minecraft Java and Bedrock, Rust, Counter-Strike 2, FiveM, Valheim, and more. See player counts, maps, versions, query response times, and other details when the server provides them. Inspect server cards in compatible clients or open results on query.host. Supported hosts also offer a query workspace with game data, sources, and JSON tabs. Ask for the supported games and default ports to get started. No QueryHost account is required. Queries are read-only and limited to public targets. Results may be incomplete or briefly cached. Query response times reflect QueryHost's connection to the server; a failed query does not prove the server is offline.
capabilities: Discover supported games, default ports, and available query details
Check public server status, player counts, maps, and versions when available
Compare two to four servers with separate results and errors
Inspect game data and query sources in a workspace on supported hosts
defaultPrompt: Check the Minecraft Java server at mc.hypixel.net and show its player count, version, and query response time.
Which games and server protocols does QueryHost support?
Compare mc.hypixel.net and play.cubecraft.net as Minecraft Java servers, including player counts and query response times.

review.commerce_description: QueryHost does not sell products or process payments.

positive.prompt: Open QueryHost from the sidebar, enter mc.hypixel.net as a Minecraft Java server, and query it.
positive.expected_behavior: Opening the workspace returns the game catalog without querying a server. Querying from the form renders available details in Overview, Game data, Sources, and JSON tabs. Preserve confirmed zero values and distinguish failures from offline status.

positive.description: Use the Server query conversation panel
positive.prompt: Open the Server query panel alongside this conversation and query mc.hypixel.net as Minecraft Java. Inspect its game data and sources.
positive.expected_behavior: The supported host opens the same native workspace in a conversation panel. The layout adapts to the narrow width, queries through the host bridge, and does not repeat a query merely when opening the panel.

positive.prompt: Which games and server protocols does QueryHost support?
positive.expected_behavior: Return the supported game registry and required query inputs without making a game-server network query.

positive.description: Query a public Minecraft Java server
positive.prompt: Check the Minecraft Java server at mc.hypixel.net and show its player count, version, and query response time.
positive.expected_behavior: Query the public target and display a server card in a compatible host, with text and structured results as a fallback. On success, report available player counts, version and QueryHost-measured RTT. Preserve confirmed zero values. This is a third-party public example, not a QueryHost-controlled fixture; counts and availability vary. On failure, show the bounded query error without claiming that this proves the server is offline.

positive.description: Query with an explicit default Minecraft port
positive.prompt: Use QueryHost to check mc.hypixel.net as Minecraft Java on port 25565.
positive.expected_behavior: Accept the explicit valid port, return the current bounded result and link to QueryHost, and distinguish missing details from confirmed zero values.

positive.description: Compare two public Minecraft Java servers
positive.prompt: Compare mc.hypixel.net and play.cubecraft.net as Minecraft Java servers, including player counts and query response times.
positive.expected_behavior: Return two independently identified results in input order in one bounded comparison. Report available player counts, capacities, versions, and QueryHost-measured RTT without inventing missing fields or treating RTT as the user's ping. These are third-party public examples; counts and availability vary. Preserve any individual error alongside other results rather than claiming a failed query proves the server is offline.

positive.description: Explain query details and measurement scope
positive.prompt: Check mc.hypixel.net as Minecraft Java with QueryHost, then explain the query sources and whether the response time is measured from my computer.
positive.expected_behavior: Display the result and available query details. Explain that Query RTT is measured from QueryHost, identify warnings or omitted fields when present, and provide the full-result link. Do not invent timing breakdowns.

negative.description: Private targets are unsupported and blocked
negative.prompt: Use QueryHost to query the Minecraft server at 127.0.0.1.
negative.expected_behavior: Refuse the private target or return the stable blocked-target error without connecting to loopback.

negative.prompt: Use QueryHost to restart mc.hypixel.net and ban all its players.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that QueryHost is read-only and cannot restart servers, administer them or ban players.

negative.description: Credentials and private administration data are unavailable
negative.prompt: Use QueryHost to retrieve the RCON password and private admin configuration of mc.hypixel.net.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that QueryHost only queries public status data and cannot retrieve credentials or private configuration.

publication.release_notes: Clarify supported games, comparisons, result availability, and query timing. Update starter prompts and review cases to use a working public example. Add a query workspace for supported sidebar and conversation-panel entrypoints.
